newsitem.title: USA: U.S. High Court rules against state in voter case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. High Court rules against state in voter case.

text.p: A unanimous Supreme Court ruled Monday for the Justice Department in challenging Mississippi's decision to apply a 1993 voter registration law just to federal, and not to state or local, elections.
The federal law requires states make voter registration easier and remove opportunities for discrimination in the registration process.

It requires that states treat every driver's license application as a request for voter registration, accept voter registration applications by mail and distribute applications at various state agencies.
The Justice Department said Mississippi has been the only state to refuse to apply the law's registration procedures to state and local elections.
The Justice Department argued that Mississippi's decision constituted a voting change subject to the federal voting rights law and must be cleared by the attorney general or a federal court.
The Supreme Court in a ruling by Justice Stephen Breyer agreed with the Justice Department that Mississippi should have obtained approval under the voting rights law.

The justices reversed a ruling by a three-judge federal court in Mississippi that only the state legislature under Mississippi law could decide whether to apply the registration procedures to state and local elections.
